drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: An item before anything else, and it is the first official sample from the exam guide.
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Open the regulation and read the subsection. Which is B.
drills.stem: An associate asks Claude to summarize a new regulation, and Claude produces a confident summary citing a specific subsection number. Before sending the summary to the compliance team, what is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Send it as-is, since Claude expressed high confidence
options.B: Verify the cited subsection against the official regulation text before sharing
options.C: Ask Claude to rate its own confidence and send it if the rating is high
options.D: Reword the summary to sound more formal, then send it

drills.why: A specific-looking citation is the detail a model can invent, and compliance will act on it. Self-rated confidence is not evidence; rewording is polish.

drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A dropdown item. A marketing lead has a customer newsletter
drills.prompt: A Claude-drafted customer newsletter. For each, choose "check against a source" or "a read-through is enough": 1. A competitor's market-share percentage. 2. Tone and length of the opening paragraph. 3. A quote attributed to a named industry analyst. 4. Three subject lines to choose from.
drills.answer: 1. Check against a source. 2. Read-through. 3. Check against a source. 4. Read-through. Specific, checkable claims get checked; style gets read.

drills.label: Sample item
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. The second official sample.
drills.answer_line: SAM: It has. B: a faster, lower-cost model
drills.stem: An associate needs to generate a high volume of short customer-reply drafts where speed and cost matter more than deep reasoning. Which choice best fits the task?

options.A: Use the most capable, highest-cost model for every reply to maximize quality
options.B: Use a faster, lower-cost model suited to straightforward, high-volume tasks
options.C: Disable all product features to reduce cost
options.D: Switch to a different AI platform

drills.why: The stem ranks speed and cost above deep reasoning. Keep the most capable model for complex work; C and D never touch the trade-off.

drills.label: Sample item
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. The third official sample.
drills.answer_line: SAM: So B. The trends survive without names and account numbers
drills.stem: A project manager wants to upload a spreadsheet containing customer names and account numbers so Claude can analyze trends. Organizational policy restricts sharing regulated personal data. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Upload the file as-is, since the analysis is internal
options.B: Remove or anonymize the personal identifiers before uploading, consistent with policy
options.C: Upload the file but instruct Claude not to retain it

drills.why: The policy controls what is shared, so the fix is in the data before upload. A request not to retain is not the control; skipping abandons a task with a safe route.

drills.question_line: SAM: One more pass. Pause and name the four parts of the game plan
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Sixty items in a hundred and twenty minutes, pass at seven hundred and twenty
drills.prompt: Name the four parts of the game plan: the paper, the clock, the formats and the method.
drills.answer: 60 items, 120 minutes, pass at 720, Output Evaluation biggest at 21%. 1:23, 0:47 and 0:10 left at items 20, 40, 60. Multiple choice, multiple response, dropdown statements. Ask, stakes, step, strike.
